responsibility: This module contains GCC’s core language-independent tree and GIMPLE infrastructure: the fundamental tree IR definition itself, the generic support libraries that manipulate it, and many central middle-end analyses and lowering passes built directly on that representation. At its base are the tree node model and metadata in tree-core.h, tree.h, tree.def, treestruct.def, and tree.cc, along with generic statement-list iteration, pretty-printing, structural dumping, diagnostics, hashing, and pass framework support. Around that core it provides the shared machinery that makes tree-based optimization possible, including CFG construction and cleanup, PHI management, SSA construction and destruction, generic data-flow utilities, exception-handling bookkeeping, inlining/body copying, and LTO tree streaming. It also hosts a broad set of tree-level analyses and canonical transformations that are not confined to a narrower loop or target submodule, such as scalar evolution and CHREC support, affine and data-reference analysis, VRP/object-size reasoning, complex and nested-function lowering, stdarg and emulated TLS lowering, switch/tailcall/NRV/SRA transformations, profiling instrumentation, and loop-oriented passes like if-conversion, distribution, predictive commoning, and auto-parallelization. Overall, this is the central shared tree middle-end substrate that defines and maintains GCC’s tree/SSA world and performs many of the compiler’s generic tree-based analyses, rewrites, and serialization tasks.
